stories.title: Holdings-first home with the top 5 per segment
stories.story: As the owner, I want a home view that shows my holdings and the five best-ranked listings in each segment with their freshness, each one's range and uncertainty one tap in on its segment list, so that I see what I own and what else is worth watching in one place.

positive: The home view shows the owner's holdings first, with their ranges, and the top 5 per segment below (owner, 3 November 2026, MP-177).
Each holding shows its value in GBP with its local currency, its latest forecast range for the chosen horizon, its suggested action with reasons, and how fresh its price is.

Each segment shows its top 5 from the versioned ranking (PH06-S05): US large caps, US tech, India Nifty 50, India midcap, US ETFs, UK ETFs, India ETFs, and gold and silver; there is no UK FTSE segment, and UK holdings still appear. Each listing's range sits on its segment list, one tap in from the home view. OWN-22, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "One tap in, reword MP-153" (pressed on the page). The option read: "Home A keeps its tiles, Home B keeps its rows, and MP-153 says the range sits on the segment list."

Every row shows its data freshness and provider status, and the cost view is one tap away (PH06-S03). Freshness is measured against the limits the owner approved; the close grace has no figure yet. OWN-07, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Approve the proposed limits now" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options").
The view reads one published version of holdings, forecasts and rankings, so every row agrees.
negative: A listing without a complete combined score shows as not ranked with the parts it has, and a segment with fewer than five ranked listings shows fewer; nothing is filled in to make five.
Risk, staleness or a provider outage is never hidden behind a loading state.
The view says it is decision support, not advice, and offers no trade.
recovery: If a read fails, the view shows the last loaded version with its age and a retry; it never mixes two versions.
After an SSE notice of a new version, the client re-reads durable state.

stories.authority: The owner reads. The view writes nothing. Code computes every value and ranking.
states: partial (a segment or holding unavailable, with its reason)
evidence: A web state matrix covering every state above on synthetic data
A version-consistency test: one read pins one published version
Playwright and axe-core checks on the built view

stories.title: Search, filters and watchlists over the discovery universe
stories.story: As the owner, I want to search and filter my holdings, watch-only listings and the curated universe of about 150 names, compare peers and benchmarks, and keep saved watchlists, so that I can explore candidates without holding them.

positive: Search and filters cover holdings, watch-only listings and the curated discovery universe by name, symbol, market, segment and kind.
A candidate shows its peers, its benchmark and the change it would make to current overlap and concentration, computed by code.
Saved watchlists are versioned per owner and environment; themes appear once dated theme membership exists (PH09-S02).
negative: A listing outside the catalogue is added only through the chat proposal, coverage check and owner confirm (PH05-S11); search cannot add it directly.
A listing with unverified rights or coverage shows as unavailable with its reason, never with made-up data.
recovery: A failed watchlist save leaves the previous version and shows the failure; the retry is idempotent.

stories.authority: The owner searches and edits watchlists. Adding to the catalogue needs the owner's confirm through PH05-S11. No agent edits a watchlist.
evidence: Search and filter cases on the synthetic catalogue
Overlap and concentration figures matching the deterministic reference
Watchlist save, conflict and retry cases

stories.title: Spend and budget on the main dashboard
stories.story: As the owner, I want to see this month's spend from the main dashboard, by environment and by part, against the £100 ceiling and its thresholds, so that cost never surprises me.

positive: The view shows dev and prod spend for AWS, market data, and Claude and evaluations against the £70 plan (data £30, AWS £22, Claude and evaluations £15, forecast and price uncertainty £3), the £30 reserve and the £60, £75 and £85 thresholds.
It separates internal estimates (live), Anthropic usage (every six hours) and reconciled billing (daily), and states the lag of each.
The top-5 scan's Claude spend shows against its £5 cap.
If the owner ever joins the Apple Developer Program, its fee month shows the fee as the one allowed exception and admits optional work on the month without the fee (COST-Q4).
negative: An unknown or unreconciled amount is shown as unknown, never as zero.
The cost view is never only in admin; it is one tap from the home view.
recovery: When the cost collector fails, the view shows the last reconciled figures with their age and a stale label.

stories.authority: The owner reads. The prod collector reads billing through a read-only role. No client changes a budget here; budget changes are settings (PH05-S14).
evidence: Threshold cases at £59.99, £60, £75 and £85 on synthetic spend
A lag and staleness case for each of the three cost sources
An Apple fee month case showing the exception and the admission basis

stories.title: Static SvelteKit PWA shell with authenticated data and private caching
stories.story: As the owner, I want a fast installable web app that holds no private data in its build and clears what it cached when I sign out, so that I can use MP safely on a laptop, an iPad or a phone.

positive: The shell is a prebuilt static SvelteKit PWA served by CloudFront from a private S3 origin with origin access control; private data and commands go through the authenticated FastAPI under /api/v1.

The service worker caches only the shell and approved non-sensitive assets; private responses are cached only as the offline policy allows and are cleared on sign-out, session expiry and account change. A browser keeps the same five kinds of data as the Apple app, each with its age. MP40-Q12c, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Both keep the five" (pressed on the page). The option read: "A browser keeps the same five kinds, each with its age, as the web frames draw now." How a browser would protect them is unverified and needs an architecture answer before build.
Typed API clients are generated from FastAPI's OpenAPI schema, and every error carries a code, a message, the request_id and the trace_id.
First paint and time to interactive are measured against agreed budgets.
negative: No financial record, secret or owner data appears in the public build or the CDN cache.
No SvelteKit server runtime, server session or SSR action is assumed.
The architecture Site in site/ does not count as the PWA.
recovery: A new shell version is picked up on the next load; a client on an incompatible API version is told to refresh rather than failing silently.
Offline, the shell shows cached views with their ages and refuses writes.

stories.authority: The owner signs in; Cognito and the API authorise every private read and command. The shell holds no authority of its own.
evidence: Build inspection proving no private data in the static output
Sign-out and session-expiry cache-clearing tests
Playwright with ARIA snapshots and axe-core checks, and the measured first paint

stories.title: Versioned ranking policy: eligibility, the 35/40/25 score and the top 5 per segment
stories.story: As the owner, I want rankings computed by a versioned, deterministic policy that combines growth, protection and opportunity only when all three are eligible, so that a top 5 means the same thing every day and can be checked.

positive: A ranking policy version holds the component definitions, normalisation, the weights (growth 35, protection 40, opportunity 25), the tie-break and the action bands.
Eligibility and abstention run before combination, and the combined score exists only when all three components are eligible (POLICY-006).
After each daily issuance, code ranks each segment's eligible listings and stores the top 5 as a versioned view, with one list each for US, UK and India ETFs (owner, 3 November 2026).

Growth and protection come from the 3, 6 and 12-month forecasts and only the opportunity component uses shorter horizons; the lists are re-ranked daily after issuance (owner, 3 November 2026, MP-177). Any missing or split 3, 6 or 12-month forecast takes both growth and protection, so the listing is not ranked. OWN-17, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Both parts go" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options"). The option read: "Any missing or split 3, 6 or 12-month forecast takes both growth and protection, so the name is not ranked."
Deterministic reference outputs for a synthetic universe reproduce exactly.
negative: A missing component is never zero and never reweighted; that listing is not ranked. A listing not ranked shows no action until it can be ranked again, with the reason. OWN-20, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "No score, no action" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options").

Gold and silver stay unavailable for formal tasks, with a reason, until the first month proves Twelve Data's cover and bar time; each day's value is then the provider's daily bar, with its boundary recorded (SCI-D08). OWN-26, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Use the provider's daily bar" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options").

No action band classifies a listing until evaluation supports the thresholds and the owner approves a ranking policy version; normalisation, ties and the threshold values stay open (FIN-OD-07). OWN-09, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Evidence first" (pressed on the page).
A 1 to 20-session forecast never feeds the growth or protection component.
recovery: A failed ranking run leaves the previous view current with its date; a re-run for the same issuance gives the same view.
A corrected forecast produces a new ranking version, and the earlier version stays for audit.

stories.authority: Code ranks. The owner approves each policy version and any change to weights, normalisation, ties or bands. No agent can change a ranking.
states: stale (no issuance since the last close)
evidence: A missing, conflicting and tied case matrix
Deterministic reference outputs for the synthetic universe
The owner's approval record for the policy version

stories.title: Suggested actions with reasons, uncertainty, portfolio impact and horizon
stories.story: As the owner, I want each holding and candidate to carry a suggested action (add, hold, pause, trim or rebalance for a holding; watch for a candidate) with its reasons, uncertainty, portfolio impact and horizon, so that I can decide with the evidence in front of me.

positive: Holdings and candidates are visibly distinct; each action shows its reasons, uncertainty and horizon and the counterfactual change to concentration and risk, computed by code.
Each action names the policy version, components, sources and model versions behind it.

Every candidate reads Watch, and the word buy is not used. OWN-03, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Watch only" (pressed on the page). The option read: "Every candidate reads Watch, and MP-144 drops the word buy."
negative: No action executes a trade, places an order, assumes a tax rule or changes contributions, and there is no sell-everything instruction.

No action label appears until evaluation supports the thresholds and the owner approves a ranking policy version; until then a listing shows its component evidence and no action label rather than a guessed one (FIN-OD-07). OWN-09, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Evidence first" (pressed on the page). The option read: "No label appears until evaluation supports the thresholds and you approve a ranking policy version."

A holding not ranked shows no action until it can be ranked again, with the reason. OWN-20, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "No score, no action" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options"). The option read: "A holding not ranked shows no action until it can be ranked again, with the reason."

Wherever the rules and the model point different ways at 3, 6 or 12 months, that horizon is conflicted and no action is ranked there. OWN-32, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Conflict at every long horizon" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options"). The option read: "Wherever the rules and the model point different ways at 3, 6 or 12 months, that horizon is conflicted and no action is ranked there."
recovery: When an input becomes stale or ineligible after publication, the action is marked stale with its reason until the next ranking run.

stories.authority: Code proposes; the owner decides and acts outside MP. Nothing in MP acts on a suggestion.
states: conflicted (rules and model point different ways at 3, 6 or 12 months; no action at that horizon)
evidence: Action cases for holdings and candidates on synthetic data
Counterfactual impact figures matching the deterministic reference
A no-trade test: no endpoint or payload can carry an order

stories.title: Rules, models and Claude views side by side, with the experimental contribution split
stories.story: As the owner, I want the rules view, the model view and the Claude-assisted reading shown separately with their disagreements, so that one score can never hide a conflict or a missing input.

positive: Rules (with their heuristic strength labelled), numerical models (with calibrated ranges) and the Claude-assisted explanation appear as separate views for the same listing and horizon.
Disagreement between rules and models is shown with each side's evidence.
The rules-versus-models contribution split is shown live from launch, labelled experimental, with no probability of its own (owner, 3 November 2026).
An F7 contribution policy appears, labelled experimental and as a simulation, only after it beats the simple comparator rules for 8 weeks in replay and shadow and the owner says yes.
negative: An unavailable input or view shows as unavailable and is never folded into a single score.
The Claude view never shows a number that a code result did not supply.
An F7 simulation is never shown as a trade, an order or an instruction.
recovery: If one view fails, the others still show, with the failed view's reason.

stories.authority: Code computes the rules, the models, the split and the F7 simulations; Claude writes words only. Only the owner switches on an F7 policy.
evidence: Agree, disagree and one-side-unavailable cases on synthetic data
A test that the split carries the experimental label and no probability
An F7 gate test: no policy shows before 8 qualifying weeks and the owner's yes

stories.title: Forecast views for every horizon from the next day to 12 months, with every state
stories.story: As the owner, I want each horizon's forecast shown with its cutoff, range, uncertainty, eligibility and evidence, and an honest state when there is no forecast, so that I never mistake a stale or unqualified view for a current one.

positive: Sections cover the next day; 5, 10 and 20 trading days; and 3, 6 and 12 calendar months, each with as-of time, data cutoff, target, range or probability, calibration, model version and evidence.
Every number identifies its task, as-of time, source and model, and says whether it is evaluated, illustrative or a scenario.
Range and fan charts have text alternatives, and both the simple and the technical mode keep material uncertainty.

Daily forecasts carry on past the £85 line; cost_paused shows only where a forecast needs the optional paid work that stopped. OWN-25, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Daily forecasts keep running" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options"). The option read: "At £85 optional paid work stops and daily forecasts carry on. Cost paused shows only where a forecast needs that paid work."
negative: A horizon with no qualified model is never removed and never given a made-up probability; it shows the rules with their heuristic strength, in_practice, or unavailable with reasons.
Offline or stale data never appears as fresh analysis.
recovery: When a forecast is corrected, the view shows the new version and annotates the old one; the original is never rewritten.

stories.authority: The owner reads. Code issues every forecast; nothing on this view changes one.
states: cost_paused (only where a forecast needs optional paid work stopped at £85)
evidence: A per-horizon state inventory rendered on synthetic data
Text alternatives checked for every chart
A join test between forecast API payloads and the view

stories.title: Proof and track record behind each forecast
stories.story: As the owner, I want to open the proof behind a forecast (its data, folds, baselines, matured outcomes and limits) so that I can judge how far to trust it.

positive: The proof shows the dataset version, folds, baseline comparison, number of matured outcomes, coverage, eligibility and limitations, and annotates corrected outcomes.
Model sheets and the regime, analog, event and pattern sheets are reachable from a forecast; the analog sheet shows its matched days since 2015 and the number of cases.
Hit rate always appears with calibration, error, coverage, turnover and the benchmark.
negative: No track record is claimed for a horizon before its outcomes mature; a 12-month record waits a year.
A judge or evaluation score is never shown as forecast accuracy.
Evidence from fewer than 20 non-overlapping blocks is labelled exploratory.
recovery: If the proof fails to load, the forecast still shows with 'proof unavailable' and a retry; a revised outcome creates a new score version shown beside the old one.

stories.authority: The owner reads. Code grades outcomes; nobody edits a past score.
evidence: Proof payload examples for an eligible, an awaiting-maturity and an exploratory forecast
Accessible text alternatives for every proof chart
A test that hit rate never renders without its companion measures

stories.title: Three and five year scenarios with editable assumptions
stories.story: As the owner, I want downside, central and upside scenarios for three and five years with assumptions I can edit, so that I can explore long-term outcomes without mistaking them for forecasts.

positive: Downside, central and upside templates cover 3 and 5 years, with explicit return, inflation, FX, contribution, fee and dividend-treatment assumptions, computed by deterministic arithmetic (POLICY-004).
The owner can edit a copy of any template; edited assumptions are labelled as the owner's.
Scenarios sit in their own section, separate from the evaluated forecasts up to 12 months.
negative: No scenario carries a probability, and 'central' never means most likely.

Template values are not used until the owner approves them (SCI-D06). A separate piece of work proposes each template value with its evidence, and the owner approves them. OWN-10, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Sourced proposal, then approve" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options").
No 12-month model output is extrapolated to make a scenario.
recovery: An invalid assumption is refused with its reason and the last saved assumptions are kept; approving new template values creates a new version.

stories.authority: The owner edits their own assumptions and approves template values. Code computes every path.
evidence: Arithmetic cases against hand-worked synthetic examples
A test that no scenario payload carries a probability
Template approval and versioning cases

stories.title: The 07:30 London daily brief
stories.story: As the owner, I want an action-first brief at 07:30 London time with each market's timestamp, priorities, risks, changes and upcoming events, so that I start the day knowing what matters.

positive: The brief is issued on weekdays at 07:30 Europe/London, moving with daylight saving, and leads with actions, then risks, changes and upcoming events.
It reads the stored latest eligible origin for each market and shows India, UK and US timestamps separately.

It is delivered in the app and announced by a neutral Web Push notice (PH07-S07); alerts held overnight arrive with it, and on Saturday and Sunday held alerts land in the in-app inbox at 07:30 (proposed).

No brief is issued on Saturday or Sunday, and Home says why. MP40-Q11b, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Weekdays only" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options"). The option read: "No brief on Saturday or Sunday. Home says why, and held alerts land in your inbox at 07:30 (proposed)."
negative: The brief never depends on a batch submitted that morning, and never presents the US and India as having closed at the same time.
No part of the brief executes an action.
recovery: If the text route is unavailable, a deterministic brief is issued and labelled (PH05-S08); if MP itself was down at 07:30, the brief is issued on recovery, labelled late, and never sent twice.

stories.authority: Code assembles and schedules the brief; the explanation route writes its words. The owner reads.
states: skipped_by_policy (Saturday or Sunday, Home says why)
evidence: DST-change and per-market timestamp cases
A missed-batch morning and a late-recovery morning, each issued once
A privacy check on the notice payload

stories.title: Material risk alerts with quiet hours, cooldown and deduplication
stories.story: As the owner, I want to be told promptly about a material risk to my holdings, but not woken for it, and never told twice, so that alerts stay worth reading.

positive: A material risk condition found on eligible as-of data, by the 30-minute checks or the daily run, creates one notification intent; immediate means right after detection at the cadence the data allows. Material means a line the owner sets is crossed on exposure, price move, volatility or an event flag; critical covers security and service faults only, so investment alerts wait for 07:30. MP40-Q11a, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Your lines, no investment wake-ups" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options"). The option read: "Material means a line you set is crossed on exposure, price move, volatility or an event flag. Critical covers security and service faults only, so investment alerts wait for 07:30." Each line still needs a value from the owner before build.
Quiet hours run 22:00 to 07:00 Europe/London; alerts in that window wait for the 07:30 brief unless an approved exception applies.

One push per holding, rule and severity in 24 hours, sooner only if it worsens or the cause is new; a dedup key groups repeats into one alert, every event stays in the app, and denied push falls back to the in-app inbox (PH07-S08). OWN-34, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Once in 24 hours" (by the owner's words in chat, "for the remaining pick up recommended options"). The option read: "One push per holding, rule and severity in 24 hours, sooner only if it worsens or the cause is new. Every event stays in the app."
Investment risk alerts are a separate class from operational incidents.
negative: An unavailable provider never produces an all-clear.
A push accepted by the push service is labelled a delivery attempt, not proof the owner read it.
No alert executes an action, and no alert payload carries a value or a holding.
recovery: An alert detected during an outage is delivered after recovery with its detection time; a retried send reuses the dedup key so the owner sees one alert.

stories.authority: Code detects, groups and routes alerts. The owner sets the value of each material line and approves any quiet-hour exception; critical covers security and service faults only. No agent can raise or silence an alert.
states: cooled_down (24 hours per holding, rule and severity)
evidence: Quiet-hours, DST, missed, duplicate and cooldown cases
A provider-outage case that produces no all-clear
Neutral payload examples

stories.title: Decision journal: what I did and why
stories.story: As the owner, I want to record what I did about a suggestion, and why, against the exact evidence I saw, so that I can later compare my decisions with what happened.

positive: The owner records 'I acted' or 'I chose not to' against the exact action, evidence and policy version shown. When no action is ranked, the owner can save an entry against the evidence on screen whenever it shows, and the entry records why none was. OWN-15, 5 November 2026 (MP-184): the owner picked "Any time evidence shows" (pressed on the page). The option read: "You can save an entry against the evidence on screen whenever no action is ranked, and the entry records why none was."
Entries are append-only and later joined to the matured outcomes of the forecasts they cite.
A weekly wrap-up lists the week's entries and their outcomes so far.
negative: A journal entry never changes holdings or triggers a trade; holdings change only through an approved import.
Claude may summarise entries but never writes one.
recovery: A failed save keeps the draft and retries idempotently; a correction is a new entry linked to the old one.

stories.authority: Only the owner writes entries. Code joins them to outcomes.
evidence: Entry, correction and outcome-join cases on synthetic data
A test that no journal path writes the ledger

stories.title: Web import journey on the canonical ledger contracts
stories.story: As the owner, I want to import statements, screenshots and files on the web and approve exactly what is committed, so that my holdings come in correctly without the web app keeping its own ledger rules.

positive: The web journey covers upload (CSV, Excel, PDF, screenshot and manual entry), preview, guided edits, explicit complete-group subsets (POLICY-005), approval, commit, reversal and history rebuild proposals (POLICY-012), all on PH-01's contracts unchanged.
Approval needs a fresh step-up and starts the commit within 15 minutes of the exact approved content (POLICY-001).
negative: The web app holds no ledger logic of its own; a changed or expired proposal needs a fresh approval.
An extracted draft is never shown as committed holdings.
recovery: A page reload mid-import resumes from server state; a commit failure offers an idempotent retry and never a second commit.

stories.authority: The owner uploads, edits and approves with a fresh sign-in. The controlled writer commits. No agent approves.
evidence: A trace from each web step to its PH-01 story and contract
A full journey walkthrough on synthetic files
Expiry, changed-content and reload cases

stories.title: Evidence trail from source to outcome, with deep links
stories.story: As the owner, I want to follow any figure back to its source and forward to its outcome, and to share a link that opens the same record on the web or the Apple app, so that every number can be checked.

positive: From any figure the owner can open the chain source, ledger, risk, forecast, action, outcome and audit.
Deep links resolve to durable, authorised records on the web and the Apple app; chat links open the exact evidence context.
negative: A deep link never rebuilds evidence afresh; it opens the stored record or says it is unavailable.
A link to another owner's or environment's record is refused.
Offline, cached records show their ages and writes are refused.
recovery: A link to a superseded record opens it with a pointer to its successor; an expired session asks for sign-in and then returns to the record.

stories.authority: The owner reads within their own scope. Links carry no authority of their own.
evidence: A full chain walkthrough on synthetic data
Cross-scope refusal and superseded-record cases
Offline and reconnect cases
